s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scrotal swelling with acute worsening and a palpable testicular mass
salient_findings: Firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness
Hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow on ultrasound
key_facts: 20-year history of left testicular bloating and dull pain
Acute worsening of symptoms over the past 10 days
Left testis is enlarged, firm, and smooth
Transillumination of the left testis is negative
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound shows a hypoechoic lesion in the left testis
Internal blood flow is present in the hypoechoic lesion
Serum CA19-9 level is elevated at 57.5 U/mL
Alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers are within normal limits

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common testicular cancer, matches clinical presentation of a testicular mass

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Common testicular cancer, elevated CA19-9 level supports this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with testicular swelling and a palpable mass, rare but plausible

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause testicular enlargement and have a variable ultrasound appearance

shortlist.label: Testicular teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Can present with a testicular mass and have a variable ultrasound appearance, including hypoechoic lesions

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow, acute worsening of symptoms, and elevated serum CA19-9 level are indicative of testicular cancer.

rejected.label: Epididymal cyst
rejected.why: While bilateral epididymal cysts are present, the key findings of a hypoechoic lesion in the left testis and elevated CA19-9 level point towards a testicular pathology rather than an epididymal cyst as the primary issue.
